description: Hand-maintained, sourced reference list of known Microsoft-driven Entra authentication rollout dates relevant to this toolkit's checks. Pure data, no logic - see Get-SAWTimelineMilestones.ps1 for how DaysRemaining is computed and docs/timeline-milestones-notes.md (if present) for update history. Verify against the Source URL before trusting a date - Microsoft has moved dates before, and this list is only as current as the last time someone checked.

milestones.Title: SSPR Registration Campaign Nudges Begin
milestones.Description: Microsoft's own wording is conditional, not universal: 'If your SSPR settings require users to register during sign-in, and enabled users do not have enough methods to complete SSPR, a registration campaign will prompt affected users to register methods ahead of enforcement.' That condition is the classic Password Reset > Registration admin blade's 'require users to register when signing in' toggle - not something this toolkit can read via Graph (that blade's resource, passwordresetpolicy, is not a real Graph resource - confirmed 404; see docs/references.md's reconfirmation-interval finding for the same blind spot on a sibling setting from that blade). So the impacted-user count below is an upper bound assuming that toggle is on, not a confirmed prediction - verify it in the admin center before treating this date as certain to affect this tenant. Also note this date is now AFTER the 2026-10-05 directory-sourced-contact-info cutover below, not ahead of it as originally worded here - Microsoft's source page states each date independently and doesn't say this nudge is specifically 'ahead of' that cutover; earlier revisions of this file assumed the two were sequenced nudge-then-enforce because the dates happened to fall that way (2026-08-06 then 2026-09-07). That assumption no longer holds now that Microsoft moved both dates - re-verify against the Source URL before restating a relationship between them.
milestones.ImpactMetricLabel: SSPR-enabled users not yet SSPR-registered (upper bound - assumes the classic 'require registration at sign-in' toggle is on; this toolkit can't read that setting)

milestones.Title: Automatic Passkey Enablement For SMS/Voice Users
milestones.Description: Microsoft auto-enables passkeys and flips the registration campaign to 'Microsoft managed' (targeting passkeys) for every user currently enabled for SMS or Voice in the authentication methods policy - based on policy scope, not on what else they have registered. A user who already has a passkey/WHfB/other phishing-resistant method registered is not exempt from this: Microsoft's own docs note such users 'may still receive prompts to register passkeys on eligible devices' (the per-device/browser nudge-suppression logic only skips devices where a qualifying local passkey is already present). Not blocking, and AUTH006's opt-out (passkeyDynamicMigration) defers it. See AUTH006.
milestones.ImpactMetricLabel: users with a phone-based method (SMS/Voice) still registered (upper-bound proxy for tenant-wide policy scope - Graph doesn't expose per-user AMP-scope evaluation directly, only what's registered)

milestones.Title: Customer-Managed Telecom Providers Become Reviewable (Microsoft Security Store)
milestones.Description: Microsoft publishes the telecom providers and related information in the Microsoft Security Store, so tenants with a genuine regulatory or operational need for an SMS/Voice channel can evaluate which option meets their regional and compliance requirements. This is an OPENING, not a deadline: nothing is required of anyone on this date, and it only matters to the subset of tenants that cannot move a given user segment to a phishing-resistant method. Everyone else should be treating passkeys as the migration path and can ignore this row. Verified 2026-08-09 against the Source URL: 'Beginning September 18th, 2026, review the telecom providers and related information available through the Microsoft Security Store to evaluate which option best meets your regional and compliance requirements.'
milestones.ImpactMetricLabel: users with a phone-based method (SMS/Voice) still registered - only the regulated/operational subset of these needs a telecom provider at all

milestones.Title: Customer-Managed Telecom Providers Become Configurable
milestones.Description: From this date a tenant that needs to keep SMS or voice can actually select and configure a telecom provider from the Microsoft Security Store, then stand up the carrier contract and pilot it. Note the wording carefully, because secondary write-ups have compressed this into 'organizations must configure their own telecom provider by October 30' - that is wrong and would invent a deadline that does not exist. Microsoft's own sentence is 'Beginning October 30, 2026, customers who need to continue using SMS or voice will be able to select and configure a telecom provider from the Microsoft Security Store' - the capability opens on this date. The only hard deadline remains 2027-02-01, when Microsoft-provided delivery stops. Verified 2026-08-09 against the Source URL (ms.date 2026-07-29).
milestones.ImpactMetricLabel: users with a phone-based method (SMS/Voice) still registered - only the regulated/operational subset of these needs a telecom provider at all

milestones.Title: SSPR Stops Accepting Directory-Sourced Contact Info
milestones.Description: SSPR will only accept explicitly registered authentication methods from this date. Directory-sourced attributes synced from on-premises AD (mobilePhone, businessPhone, otherMails) that were never explicitly registered stop working for SSPR verification. Date corrected from an earlier recorded value of 2026-09-07 - re-verified 2026-08-06 against the Source URL (updated by Microsoft 2026-08-04).
milestones.ImpactMetricLabel: SSPR-enabled users not yet SSPR-registered (upper-bound proxy - Graph doesn't expose whether a registered method is directory-sourced or explicit)

milestones.Title: Register Security Information CA Policies Extend To WHfB/macOS Platform SSO Registration
milestones.Description: Before this date, Conditional Access policies targeting the 'Register security information' user action did NOT evaluate during Windows Hello for Business or macOS Platform SSO credential registration - MFA was still required by default for those flows, but any stricter Grant controls (authentication strength, trusted locations, a TAP escape) on such a policy weren't enforced there. From this date they are. Widens CA004's blast radius: a policy that excludes Temporary Access Pass from its authentication strength now also blocks WHfB/macOS Platform SSO registration for TAP-only users, not just the combined registration experience - worth reviewing any Register-security-information-scoped policy if this wasn't already accounted for.

milestones.Title: Passwordless Password Change In My Sign-Ins (Late October 2026)
milestones.Description: Exact date not yet published by Microsoft as of this writing - 'late October 2026' per Message Center MC1437671, shown here as the last day of that month as an upper-bound estimate. Off by default, tenant-wide only (no pilot/group targeting), admin activation required. No Graph API exists yet to check this in the toolkit - supported APIs are promised 'at release'. Revisit once it ships.

milestones.Title: System-Preferred Authentication (Microsoft Managed) Gradual Rollout Completes
milestones.Description: Not a hard cutover date - Microsoft's own docs state the Microsoft-managed behavior (system-preferred authentication applied to BOTH first and second factor, not just second factor) 'is being gradually deployed to tenants through August 2026'. Shown here as the last day of that window as an upper-bound estimate. System-Preferred Authentication is a distinct policy (systemCredentialPreferences) from the registration campaign covered elsewhere here - it controls what gets PRESENTED at sign-in for an already-registered credential, not what gets nudged for registration. Once fully rolled out, a tenant that has never touched this setting (state 'default') starts presenting the strongest registered method (ranked: TAP, then passkey, then CBA, then Authenticator, then others) at BOTH first and second factor, which can be a surprising change in what users see at sign-in if nobody was told to expect it. See the Authentication Methods Policy Inventory section for this tenant's actual configured state.

milestones.Title: Windows Hello for Business / macOS Platform SSO Become Standalone MFA Factors
milestones.Description: Per Message Center MC1450134, Entra begins recognising Windows Hello for Business and macOS Platform SSO as standalone MFA factors: they already satisfied MFA at primary sign-in, but users could still be asked for a separate passkey for step-up authentication or an Authentication Strength check. After this change they can complete supported MFA challenges without one. Rollout stated as early October 2026 through late November 2026 - shown here as the end of that window as an upper-bound estimate, not a hard cutover. Microsoft states no configuration change is required, but there is a real side effect worth planning for: users holding ONLY these device-bound credentials will no longer receive automatic prompts to register additional MFA methods. That population previously self-corrected via those prompts and now won't, while remaining unable to complete MFA from any device that doesn't carry the credential. See the WHfB-Only (Not Portable) badge in the Security Info Registration Triage section for exactly who that is in this tenant, and treat a portable backup method (a synced passkey, or a passkey in Authenticator) as the mitigation.
milestones.ImpactMetricLabel: users whose only phishing-resistant method is device-bound Windows Hello for Business (no portable method as backup)

milestones.Title: Passkey Registerable As A First MFA Method (Phase 1: Passkeys/FIDO2)
milestones.Description: Per Message Center MC1450133, users can register a passkey or passwordless method as their FIRST multifactor method, rather than having to set up a weaker method first. Microsoft's framing: password-only users can go straight to a passkey, making it easier to adopt strong authentication from day one. Phase 1 covers synced passkeys, Entra passkeys on Windows and FIDO2 security keys, stated as mid-October 2026 through mid-November 2026 - shown here as mid-November as an upper-bound estimate. This narrows, but does not remove, the bootstrap problem BOOT001 describes: it helps a user who already HAS a password and needs to add MFA, whereas a genuinely new user with no credential at all still needs a Temporary Access Pass or admin provisioning to get in far enough to register anything. Microsoft's own recommended actions for this change include requiring MFA for security info registration, which is what CA005 checks.

milestones.Title: Passkey Registerable As A First MFA Method (Phase 2: WHfB, macOS Platform SSO, Authenticator)
milestones.Description: Phase 2 of MC1450133, extending first-method registration to Windows Hello for Business, macOS Platform SSO and Microsoft Authenticator passwordless sign-in. Stated as early January 2027 through late February 2027 - shown here as the end of that window as an upper-bound estimate. Note this phase lands AFTER the 2027-02-01 SMS/Voice retirement below, so it does not help with that deadline: plan phone-based migration on the Phase 1 methods (passkeys/FIDO2) and on Temporary Access Pass, not on this date.

milestones.Title: Microsoft-Provided SMS/Voice Retirement (No Opt-Out)
milestones.Description: Microsoft-provided SMS and voice delivery retires outright. There is no opt-out for this date - AUTH006's opt-out only defers the 2026-09-01 automatic enablement above, not this one. Narrower criterion than that milestone: only users whose ONLY available MFA method is SMS/Voice (no Authenticator, no passkey, nothing else registered) will be blocked with a mandatory passkey registration prompt - a user who also has another method registered is unaffected by this specific date, even though they'd still count toward the 2026-09-01 impact number above.
milestones.ImpactMetricLabel: users whose only registered MFA method is SMS/Voice (no other method, phishing-resistant or otherwise)
